title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a single computational sketch page, wedged between two administrative documents dated 1979–80. It sits in the 'Teichmüller groupoids' dossier.

**Setting.** Take a 3-element set {i,j,k} with basis vectors e_i, e_j, e_k in Z^3. Let ω, ω' = −ω be its two cyclic orientations. The note defines ω_{ij} as the orientation with ω_{ij}(j) = i.

**The vectors.** The plane involved is {x : Σx = 0}, twisted by the orientation (sign) character of S_3; this is what the '∧ω' notation encodes.
- The R̃_i = (e_j − e_k) ∧ ω_{jk} are the six short roots ±R̃_i of an A_2 system. They are made independent of choices by tensoring with the orientation that fixes the sign of e_j − e_k.
- The Q̃_i^ω = R̃_{ω²i} − R̃_{ωi} = (e_j + e_k − 2e_i) ∧ ω are the six long roots. Together the 12 vectors form the G_2 root configuration, i.e. the 12 rational directions of the hexagonal lattice.
- Q̃^{ω'} = −Q̃^ω, so an orientation reversal is the same as a sign change.

**The operator i_ω.** It is a 'complex structure' on the plane determined by the orientation: i_ω Q̃_i^ω = R̃_i and i_ω R̃_i = −Q̃_i^ω = Q̃_i^{ω'}. It is quarter-turn rotation (multiplication by ±i, after the √3 normalisation), essentially (ω − ω²)/√3 with ω the order-3 rotation. This is the CM-by-Z[ζ_3] structure of the hexagonal lattice.

**The diagram.** It is the circle of rays (directions) of this plane, with the 12 directions in cyclic order.
- Q̃_k^{ω'}, ±R̃, Q̃^{ω}, … alternate at 30° steps.
- Each short-root point ±R̃_i is 'blown up' (small semicircle) into three nearby points R̃_i^{ω}, R̃_i, R̃_i^{ω'}, giving 24 marked points.
- Pencil chords join ±R̃ points in a hexagram pattern. These look like the triangles/hexagons of the hexagonal lattice, or the chords related by the order-3 and order-2 symmetries.

**Likely purpose.** Within the dossier this serves the study of the genus-0, 4-point / genus-1, 1-point Teichmüller groupoids and their symmetry groups. The hexagonal lattice is the elliptic curve with j = 0, i.e. the order-3 orbifold point of M_{1,1}. Its 12 cusp-like directions and the S_3 = Aut{i,j,k} action describe a combinatorial model (a cell or tessellation picture) on which the groupoid acts. The tripled points with semicircles suggest a real oriented blow-up at the orbifold or special points. The exact purpose cannot be fully determined from this page alone.
errors: Normalisation: with R_i = e_j − e_k and Q_i = R_{ω²i} − R_{ωi}, the linear map sending R_i ↦ −Q_i forces Q_i ↦ −3R_i (up to sign), not R_i. So i_ω² = −3 on the integral vectors. The relations i_ωQ̃ = R̃ and i_ωR̃ = −Q̃ hold only up to a positive scalar, i.e. as identities of rays on the circle, or after rescaling i_ω by 1/√3.

Sign convention: with (i,j,k) cyclic for ω, R_{ω²i} − R_{ωi} = 2e_i − e_j − e_k = −(e_j + e_k − 2e_i). The last line's sign therefore depends on how '∧ω' / ω_{jk} are normalised; the conventions are not fixed on the page.

Notation drift: R̃_i^ω is defined via ω_{jk}, which does not depend on ω. Yet the diagram distinguishes R̃_i^ω, R̃_i, R̃_i^{ω'} as three distinct nearby points. The superscripted R̃'s in the picture presumably denote blown-up or perturbed directions not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Short and long roots of A_2 forming the 12 directions of the hexagonal lattice, twisted by the orientation (sign) character of S_3 to make them canonical
ideas.modern_name: G_2 root system / Eisenstein lattice Z[ζ_3] with S_3 ⋉ μ_6 symmetry; sign-twisted standard representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Killing–Cartan); the sign-twist convention is folklore

ideas.what: Orientation-dependent complex structure i_ω (quarter-turn rotation) exchanging short and long root directions
ideas.modern_name: CM structure of the j=0 elliptic curve; (ω−ω²)/√3

ideas.what: Circle of directions with 12 special rays and the short-root points blown up into triples (semicircles), as a combinatorial picture for Teichmüller-groupoid / M_{0,4}–M_{1,1} considerations
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / boundary circle model for the orbifold point of order 3 of M_{1,1}; dessin-like picture
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (cf. Esquisse d'un programme discussion of T_{0,4}, T_{1,1} and their special points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the genus 0/1 'modular' building blocks, but not this specific picture

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine computational sketch of the G_2/hexagonal-lattice directions with an orientation-twisted complex structure, plus a diagram whose role cannot be pinned down from the page alone. Nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The diagram labels near the top are R̃_k^ω, R̃_k, R̃_k^{ω'}; the analogous triples appear at the other ±R̃ points. The labels at left read −R̃_j^{ω'}, −R̃_j, −R̃_j^{ω} (order uncertain), consistent with the transcription.
The NB line reads 'NB ω_{ij} est l'orientation telle que ω_{ij}(j) = i'. This is correct.
'{i,j,k} = 3' likely means {i,j,k} = the 3-element set (written '3' as a set), not an equation.
